questions.question: What is the heartbeat interval used by Module 3 to send network packages to the C2 server?

points: The heartbeat package is sent every 60 seconds
The heartbeat uses Cookie fields to transmit encrypted data
Data includes: check code, process ID, system version, IP address, computer name, account, and whether it is 64-bit process
expected_answer.source_section: Section 2.7 Analysis on module 3, page 6-7

questions.question: Why did Antiy CERT classify this attack as an APT incident despite it being based on a commercial automated platform?

points: It is a targeted attack against specific Chinese government agencies (one of the features of APT)
It has anti-detection functions and can conceal itself effectively
The attack capability is close to APT-level even though it relies on automated platform rather than custom coding
It demonstrates characteristics like running in memory, no hard disk writing, multi-beacon communication, and difficulty in forensic analysis
expected_answer.source_section: Section 1 Background and Section 4 Conclusion, pages 1 and 11-12

questions.question: What command execution techniques does APT-TOCS use to deploy its malicious shellcode?

points: Uses powershell.exe to execute Shellcode scripts
Downloads encrypted data into memory for operation using PowerShell
Decrypts data using base64 decoding and Gzip decompression
Creates suspended process rundll32.exe to inject Module 3
Uses WinExec function to call powershell.exe for downloading leading data
Operates entirely in memory with no hard disk writing operations
expected_answer.source_section: Section 2.1 Leading files and sample downloading, Section 2.2 Key mechanism, Section 2.3-2.6, pages 1-5

questions.question: What evidence links the APT-TOCS attack to the Cobalt Strike penetration testing platform?

points: Module 1 contains 'Beacon' strings and comparison shows it is identical to payload generated by Cobalt Strike Beacon (except for header data, request file name, and IP address)
Module 2's disassembling commands are exactly the same as Cobalt Strike files, including XOR encryption (x86/shikata_ga_nai), DLL downloading, and function calling modes
Module 3 data package comparison shows identical GET request patterns using Cookie fields for encrypted transmission with 60-second heartbeat interval
The entire attack chain matches Cobalt Strike's Beacon mode communication pattern
expected_answer.source_section: Section 3 The authentication analysis on the technology sources of this attack, pages 7-11

questions.question: What are the key technical characteristics of the APT-TOCS attack chain and execution method?

points: Uses powershell.exe to execute Shellcode scripts for remote control

Downloads encrypted data into memory using PowerShell
Decrypted data is executable Shellcode generated by Cobalt Strike
Uses Beacon mode for communication

Transmits heartbeat package data using RSA and BASE64 encryption via Cookie fields

Module 3 data package comparison: both use Cookie to transmit encrypted information and send requests every 60 seconds
The Shellcode for communication is conducted using Beacon mode generated by Cobalt Strike platform

questions.question: What are the four stages DOPPELPAYMER ransomware executes from initial delivery to file encryption?

Stage 3: Modifies Boot Configuration Database (disables recovery, enables safeboot minimal mode, configures Group Policy to display ransom message)
Stage 4: Reboots the system and begins encrypting files with .doppeled extension

questions.question: How does Cobalt Strike's beacon communicate with the C2 server and what encryption methods are used for different operations?

points: Heartbeat: Uses HTTP cookies with RSA PKCS1 padding encrypted metadata
Tasks: Uses AES-256 in CBC mode with HMAC-SHA-256 encryption
Callbacks: HTTP POST with encrypted payload (first 4 bytes contain payload size)
AES key is calculated using first 16 bytes of decrypted metadata
Beacon configuration is XOR encrypted with static default keys per version
expected_answer.source_section: C2 Communication section, pages 10-12

CVE-2013-2460: ProviderSkeleton invoke() RCE (Java ≤ 1.7.0_21)

expected_answer.source_section: Target Module: Smart Java Applet Attack, pages 18-23

questions.question: What are the key differences between staged and stageless Cobalt Strike beacon payloads in terms of size, delivery, and execution?

points: Staged: Small initial payload that retrieves larger beacon.dll from C2, used to evade AV detection with smaller footprint
Stageless: Delivered all at once (>200KB), contains full malicious functionality without additional C2 retrieval
Both use named pipes and XOR decryption (default key 0xE3F4C314)
Both use Reflective DLL loading to load beacon into memory
Staged allows embedding in exploits with resource limitations (e.g., command line character limits)
expected_answer.source_section: Target Module: Staged/Stageless Executable Generator, pages 8-10

questions.question: What default XOR key does Cobalt Strike use to encrypt beacon configurations in version 4?

points: Default XOR key: 0xE3F4C314 for staged payloads
Default XOR key: 0x23 (35) for PowerShell HTA payloads
The XOR key is static for each respective beacon version (3 or 4)
Configuration is marked in the executable by patterns that allow parsing directly from unpacked beacon DLL
expected_answer.source_section: Staged/Stageless Executables - Beacon Configuration, page 9-10

questions.question: How does Cobalt Strike's staged payload bypass AV detection and what are the advantages over stageless payloads?

points: Staged payloads are small, leaving less of a footprint and appearing more benign
Initial payload has less functionality, more likely to evade AV detection
Larger payload (beacon.dll) is retrieved afterward and loaded directly into memory using Reflective DLL injection
Allows embedding in exploits with resource limitations on the target
Stagers can be delivered using different techniques while retrieving the same robust payload
expected_answer.source_section: Staged vs. Stageless, page 8

questions.question: What encryption methods does Cobalt Strike use for C2 communication including heartbeats, tasks, and callbacks?

points: Heartbeat data: RSA with PKCS1 padding to encrypt metadata stored in HTTP cookie
Task commands: AES-256 in CBC mode with HMAC-SHA-256
AES key calculated using the first 16 bytes of decrypted metadata
Callbacks use the same AES-256 encryption, with first 4 bytes indicating payload size
All C2 communication is encrypted to evade network detection
expected_answer.source_section: C2 Communication - Heartbeat, Tasks, Callbacks, pages 10-12

questions.question: What Java vulnerabilities are exploited by the Smart Java Applet Attack module and how does it select which exploit to use?

points: CVE-2011-3544 (Rhino script engine) - Java <= 1.6.0_27 or Java == 7.0
CVE-2013-2465 (2D ImagingLib) - Java <= 1.6.0_45
CVE-2012-4681 (SunToolkit) - Java <= 1.7.0_6
CVE-2013-2460 (ProviderSkeleton invoke()) - Java <= 1.7.0_21
Selection based on polling 'java.version' via System.getProperty and matching against version ranges
The module is 'smart' because it determines which exploit to use based on victim's Java version
expected_answer.source_section: Smart Java Applet Attack - CVE sections, pages 18-24

questions.question: What are the three main components of Cobalt Strike's architecture?

questions.question: How does Cobalt Strike's 'malleable C&C profile' feature help attackers bypass network security systems?

This disguise allows communication with attacker server without detection by network security systems
Uses a settings file called 'profile' to execute this feature

questions.question: What naming convention does the Lockean group use for the Rclone exfiltration tool?
